main_body: Multi-storey office/campus building drawn as a flat-roof slab: a roof terrace area (rows ~1-20) above a green stripe, then a front facade with four rows of windows and a ground-floor entrance.
top_band: Roof area in grey-lilac (L~168, rows 7-37 at x=32/64) with a light parapet at rows 1-2 (L=226). It reads as a roof seen from above with rooftop units, but it is about 30 rows tall and is separated from the facade only by a thin green line, so it is not a foreshortened top; the facade below is a plain straight-on elevation.
evidence: The facade is a flat elevation: windows in rows, floor bands and a door painted face-on with no overhang or eave shadow. The roof is drawn as a large flat plan area stacked above it (about 30 rows) with rooftop vents and a skylight. That is a top-down plan stacked on a front elevation rather than a foreshortened 3/4 top over a front face. The only real top band is the 2-row light parapet (L=226), a rim that is too thin. The windows are flat glass with only light frames and no deep inner shadow. Fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 32 distinct colours and a median of 9 per tile, against 66-185 colours and 11-18 per tile for the references. It is clearly lower in colour count and a bit lower per tile. Concrete speckle on the roof and wall panels and diagonal glass highlights give some texture, and flat-fill coverage is 9% against 0% for the references. The outline is tinted rather than neutral black (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels). The facade wall ramp has only about 3-4 steps, and the windows repeat as identical copies. Next to the richly shaded tiled roofs and half-timber of the references, it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails.
